items.title: Measuring the Cross-Lingual Comprehension Gap: How the language of the evidence shapes what language models understand
items.description:
arXiv:2608.06506v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models are often evaluated as though capabilities demonstrated in English remain equally available when the same content is presented in other languages. Traditional multilingual benchmarks rarely isolate language while holding content, quest
items.summary: A study highlights that language models perform differently when processing content in different languages, challenging the assumption that their abilities in one language directly translate to others. This finding underscores the need for more nuanced evaluations of cross-lingual comprehension capabilities.
items.summary_detailed: The study highlights a significant gap in cross-lingual comprehension among language models, revealing that these models often perform differently when processing content in non-English languages compared to English, despite similar surface-level evaluations. Researchers argue that current multilingual benchmarks inadequately assess true linguistic capabilities by not sufficiently isolating the impact of language from the content. This finding has broader implications for the development and deployment of language models, suggesting a need for more nuanced evaluation methods to ensure equitable performance across languages.
items.summary_bullets:
• Language model performance can vary significantly across different languages.
• Traditional benchmarks do not adequately separate the effects of language from content.
• The comprehension gap between English and other languages exists in language models.
• Evaluating language models requires more nuanced approaches to isolate linguistic factors.
